preset.title: The Wrong Reflection
preset.description: A candlelit mirror reflection smiles and tilts independently while the real person stays still.

data.instructions_markdown:
# Higgsfield preset: /the-wrong-reflection

Visible effect: A candlelit mirror reflection smiles and tilts independently while the real person stays still.

Preserve: Recognizable identity, facial proportions, apparent age, underlying natural skin tone, hairstyle and gender presentation of the supplied foreground person; one coherent main subject throughout.

Use the supplied photograph as the person's identity reference. A photo plus this
slash command is the complete creative brief. Preserve apparent age, recognizable
facial proportions, natural skin tone, hairstyle and gender presentation; the emoji's
gender or skin modifier selects the same recipe and never overrides the photograph.
Use the most prominent foreground person if several are shown. If there is no person
or identity is not readable, ask for one clear portrait; do not invent a subject.

1. Reuse an already confirmed source media ID. Otherwise upload the attached photo
   once with `media_upload_and_confirm`. For a readable local file use `media_upload`,
   PUT its bytes and `media_confirm`; never invent an attachment URL or media ID.
   If no photo is accessible, call `media_upload_widget` as the only tool in that
   turn and resume this same recipe after upload. No additional written brief is needed.
2. Read `models_get` for `gpt_image_2_5` and `seedance_2_5` to verify their current
   reference roles, portrait support, duration and parameters before submitting.
   The defaults below are requested settings, not proof of live availability.
   If either model is unavailable or incompatible, report that limit before spending;
   do not silently change the model, identity workflow or paid/free mode.
3. Prepare one hidden scene start frame with `generate_image_batch`, with one
   `requests` item at stable `index:0`. Inside `params`, use model `gpt_image_2_5`,
   `variant:"flare"`, `quality:"high"`, `resolution:"2k"`, `count:1`, the final aspect ratio,
   the source photo as `medias:[{role:"image_references",value:<confirmed source media_id>}]`,
   and the preprocessing master prompt below. It establishes the person, costume,
   location and the initial effect state; it must not depict later animation events.
4. Wait with `jobs_wait` (`timeout_seconds:15`) until that exact image job completes.
   Stop on failure. If accessible, inspect the result for one recognizable subject,
   an unobstructed face, coherent anatomy and the required initial state. Do not
   claim visual inspection when unavailable. Never submit with a pending/failed frame.
5. Call `generate_video` once, putting the generation parameters below in `params`,
   `count:1`, the completed frame as `medias:[{role:"start_image",value:<completed image job_id>}]`,
   and the video master prompt below. Use `mode:"omni_reference"` for the supplied
   frame and `generate_audio:false` for silent output. Do not pass a `sound` parameter.
   Do not pass the source selfie as a second
   start frame, use a prompt/element ID as a media ID or add product-studio settings.
6. Wait for that exact video job with `jobs_wait`. Keep the auto-updating generation
   widget returned by `generate_video` as the final display; do not create a second
   display unless the user explicitly requests one. Keep the start frame internal.

Explicit user format/count/duration requests override defaults only when supported
by the selected models. Default is one silent 8-second 9:16 video at 1080p, with
audio disabled by `generate_audio:false`. Keep the identity and scene consistent
across both stages. If duration or orientation is overridden,
update those literal values in both prompts and proportionally rescale the motion
timings; preserve the scene and event order. Otherwise use the prompts unchanged.
Follow existing credit/free-generation
and tool approval gates. Reading this recipe or explaining an emoji does not submit
anything. Do not run on a quoted, translated or negated command. No extra plan,
style chooser or creative questionnaire is needed for a supplied photo and invocation.

If `preset_recommendation` explicitly returns without a submission, keep this recipe
and retry the same video arguments with its `declined_preset_id`. On timeout or an
unknown submission outcome, do not retry or spend again; use the returned job/status
or report the uncertainty. An additional paid attempt needs the user's authorization.
Do not replace a failed scene with another effect. Keep master prompts out of the
chat response and report only the real job state and result.

## Generation parameters

```json
{
  "model": "seedance_2_5",
  "aspect_ratio": "9:16",
  "duration": 8,
  "mode": "omni_reference",
  "resolution": "1080p",
  "generate_audio": false
}
```

## Master prompt

Use the supplied photograph as the identity reference for the single main person. Preserve their recognizable facial proportions, apparent age, natural skin tone, hairstyle and gender presentation. If multiple people appear in the source, use the most prominent foreground person only. Animate the supplied scene into an 8-second silent vertical shot. Keep the established over-the-shoulder mirror geometry as the camera slowly pushes toward the glass. During seconds 0–2 the reflection matches the real person’s neutral still posture. During seconds 2–6 only the reflected face develops a small deliberate smile and tilts its head slightly; the real person’s visible shoulder and back of head remain completely motionless. Candle flames flicker and faint condensation appears at mirror edges without hiding the face. Hold the impossible reflected smile toward the camera during seconds 6–8. Exactly one real person and one reflection; no additional figures, distorted face or jump cuts. Photorealistic skin, fabric and environment; coherent anatomy, restrained motion and stable identity. One continuous shot. No cuts, text, captions, logos, gore, blood, facial melting, duplicate main people or extra limbs.

## Preprocessing master prompt

Use the supplied photograph as the identity reference for the single main person. Preserve their recognizable facial proportions, apparent age, natural skin tone, hairstyle and gender presentation. If multiple people appear in the source, use the most prominent foreground person only. An over-the-shoulder portrait of the person seated before a large antique mirror in a quiet Victorian room with several candles. The real shoulder and back of head occupy the foreground; their recognizable face appears clearly in the mirror. Establish physically plausible mirror geometry, matching posture and a neutral expression. Exactly one real person and their one normal reflection, no second person behind glass. Reflection matches the still head exactly; no smile, tilt or condensation yet. One static first frame. Photorealistic cinematic materials, coherent anatomy, readable facial detail. No text, logos, gore, additional people or split-screen panels.
